learning_objective: The learner will judge whether each of eight peer review comments is useful or not useful, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** peer-feedback-judge
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether each of eight peer review comments is useful or not useful, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Peer Review, Evidence for a Score (defined in this chapter above this block or in Chapter 3). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each comment the learner commits one of two bins. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct bin column in Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Reading the three rules is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Praise is useful feedback. (2) A harsh comment is an honest one. (3) A comment needs no evidence if the reviewer is experienced. **Instructional Rationale:** Judging feedback against the three rules is an Evaluate-level action that improves the comments the learner writes. Pairs of comments about the same flaw, one useful and one not, teach the learner what the difference looks like. **Content:** The two bins: Useful, and Not useful. The eight comments (all made up, about an improved Watershed Basics component): | # | Comment | Correct bin | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Image 3 has the alt text "map". Describe what the map shows: the river and its two tributaries. | Useful | It cites the evidence and says what to do. | | 2 | The accessibility is bad. | Not useful | It has no evidence and no action. | | 3 | The quiz explanations are clear, and question 4 says why the wrong choices are wrong. | Useful | It names specific strengths that the author should keep. | | 4 | Nice work! | Not useful | It says nothing that the author can use. | | 5 | The license footer is missing on page 3, so check 6 of the open-license metric fails. Add the footer. | Useful | It ties the comment to a rubric check and an action. | | 6 | Whoever wrote this clearly does not understand watersheds. | Not useful | It attacks the person and gives no evidence. | | 7 | The reading level is grade 9 in section 3 and the audience is grade 6 to 7. Shorten the sentences there. | Useful | It cites a measurement and says what to do. | | 8 | I would have done it differently. | Not useful | It gives no reason and no direction. | **Provenance:** The comments are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The three rules follow the chapter section "Peer Review". **Rules:** Each comment has exactly one correct bin, four per bin. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one comment and the two bins. 2. The learner places the comment in a bin, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After comment 8 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 comments in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [bin]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This comment is [bin]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can give useful peer feedback." Below 7 it lists the Why text of each missed comment. **Starting State:** The first comment in the shuffled order and the two bins. The question shown is "Could the author act on this?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter gives three rules for peer review: tie comments to evidence, say what to do, and review the work and not the person.
